by_judge.judge: C M POONACHA WILL SIT IN COURT HALL NO.6 AT DHARWAD

narrative:
On August 3, 2026, the Karnataka High Court achieved a 44.5% overall hearing rate, taking up 1,103 of 2,478 scheduled cases across 40 judges. This reflects an operational rebound compared to recent sessions, surpassing the 38.1% rate recorded on July 31 (879 of 2,307 heard) and 39.5% on July 28 (1,030 of 2,610 heard), while matching the 44.5% clearance observed on July 20.

Judicial performance highlights included notable output in several court halls. In Hall 20, Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar heard 61 of 70 cases (87.1%). Justice Suraj Govindaraj processed 77 of 90 matters (85.6%) on his primary list in Hall 10, alongside 43 of 89 (48.3%) in Hall 11. Justice V Srishananda in Hall 21 addressed 70 of 104 scheduled cases (67.3%). Handling the court's heaviest single docket, Justice S Vishwajith Shetty in Hall 19 heard 95 of 300 listed cases (31.7%).

Stage-wise conversion demonstrated high efficiency in preliminary proceedings, with Preliminary Hearings reaching 61.3% (155 of 253) and Admissions converting at 52.3% (231 of 442), up from 35.4% on July 31. Orders progressed at 45.6% (401 of 879). Conversely, Final Hearing matters lagged with a 16.5% conversion rate (91 of 551), dropping from 25.5% on July 31.

In case-type distribution, Writ Petitions (WP) comprised the largest volume, with 498 of 1,111 cases heard (44.8%), showing an increase from 34.7% on July 31. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) saw 190 of 408 cases heard (46.6%), while Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) converted at 37.4% (79 of 211). Regular Second Appeals (RSA) and Family Court Revision Petitions (RPFC) recorded strong clearance at 59.1% (78 of 132) and 68.6% (24 of 35), respectively.
